study type: Descriptive study of placental tissue samples
outcome: Spatial variation in CD4+, CD3+, CD8+ T-cell distribution
Upregulation of AP-1 subunits ATF-3 and JUN, and NFKB
Enriched ITGb1 ligand receptor interactions (with fibronectin and ADAMS)
cohort: The participants were individuals with severe Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS), specifically placenta increta cases, from whom maternal-fetal interface tissue samples were collected.
finding: In placenta increta cases of severe Placenta Accreta Spectrum, the maternal-fetal interface is characterized by spatial variations in T-cell distribution, upregulation of trophoblast invasion-promoting transcription factors, increased ECM degradation, and an immunosuppressive environment with specific protein expression changes, collectively suggesting a more invasive trophoblast phenotype likely driven by fibronectin via AP-1 signalling.
cross-section timing: At the time of delivery/hysterectomy for PAS management
